title: How do six big numbers read in both systems?
description: Six numbers of seven to ten digits are cut into Indian groups and into American groups. Each is then read with its lakh, crore or arab names and with its million or billion names, and the commas are taken out again to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: cut the digits first, three then twos for the Indian system and threes for the American system, and let the group names give the reading. Ask the class how many digits the first number has before any cut is made. Watch for students who use the American threes for the Indian groups and say crore too early.

source: Figure it Out, Q1 (read and name in both systems)
video_script.why: The child has placed commas in both systems and read a ten digit number, and now does the same for six numbers.
video_script.substitution: Cut the digits into Indian groups, three and then twos, for lakh, crore and arab names, and into American groups of three for million and billion names.
video_script.anchor: Six numbers, each a string of digits, with an Indian row and an American row of group names under them.
video_script.payoff_line: Each number is now written with Indian commas and named in both systems

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the first number has seven digits. In the Indian system it reads forty lakh, fifty thousand, six hundred seventy eight.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>In the American system it reads four million, fifty thousand, six hundred seventy eight.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The second number has eight digits. In the Indian system it reads four crore, eighty one lakh, twenty one thousand, six hundred twenty.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>In the American system it reads forty eight million, one hundred twenty one thousand, six hundred twenty.

marks.m4: 246813579 is cut into 246 | 813 | 579 and named in millions

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the third number also has eight digits. In the Indian system it reads two crore, twenty two thousand, two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The lakh group is all zeros, so we skip it. In the American system it reads twenty million, twenty two thousand, two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The fourth number has nine digits. In the Indian system it reads twenty four crore, sixty eight lakh, thirteen thousand, five hundred seventy nine.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The American reading is two hundred forty six million, eight hundred thirteen thousand, five hundred seventy nine.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, the fifth number has nine digits. In the Indian system it reads thirty four crore, fifty lakh, five hundred forty three.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The thousand group is all zeros, so we skip it. In the American system it reads three hundred forty five million, five hundred forty three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The last number has ten digits. In the Indian system it reads one arab, two crore, three lakh, four thousand, fifty.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>In the American system it reads one billion, twenty million, three hundred four thousand, fifty.
